# Appeal of Denial — Lower Back Disc Surgery (CPT 63030)

**RE: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination**
**Member:** Taylor Jennings
**Member ID:** W530749089
**Reference Number:** POC-F7C299C469-49918
**Date of Denial Notice:** 2026-07-31
**Plan:** Cigna (Commercial/ACA), Illinois
**Governing Policy:** Cigna Medical Coverage Policies - Musculoskeletal: CMM-606 Lumbar Microdiscectomy (Laminotomy, Laminectomy, or Hemilaminectomy) (V1.0.2026)
URL: https://www.evicore.com/sites/default/files/clinical-guidelines/2026-04/Cigna_CMM-606%20Lumbar%20Microdiscectomy_V1.0.2026_Eff08.04.2026_Pub04.30.2026.pdf

Dear Cigna Appeals Department,

I am writing to request a reconsideration of the denial of my prior authorization request for lower back disc surgery (CPT 63030), dated 2026-07-31, reference number POC-F7C299C469-49918. My surgeon, Dr. Okafor, has documented that this procedure is medically necessary, and I believe the medical records support approval under Cigna's own published criteria.

## Why I believe this denial should be reversed

The denial notice states only that my request "does not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity." It does not identify which specific criterion was not met. I have reviewed the plan's own policy, CMM-606, and I believe my records show that the criteria for an **Initial Primary Lumbar Microdiscectomy** have been met.

The policy states:

> "Initial Primary Lumbar Microdiscectomy (Laminotomy, Laminectomy or Hemilaminectomy) CMM.SP.IN.606.2 v1.0.2026 Initial primary lumbar microdiscectomy (laminotomy, laminectomy, or hemilaminectomy) is considered medically necessary when performed for EITHER of the following conditions when ALL of the associated criteria have been met:"

The policy further states that the associated symptom pattern includes:

> "▪ symptoms worsen with standing and/or walking ▪ symptoms are alleviated with sitting and/or forward flexion • Less than clinically meaningful improvement with at least TWO of the following (unless contraindicated):"

and lists the qualifying exam/history findings as:

> "◦ positive straight leg raise ◦ positive crossed straight leg raise ◦ positive femoral stretch test ◦ dermatomal sensory deficit ◦ functionally limiting motor weakness (e.g., foot drop, quadriceps weakness) ◦ reflex changes ◦ unremitting radicular pain into the lower extremity(ies) without concordant objective exam findings"

**My records establish the following:**

- I have had 14 months of progressive lower back pain that is not relieved by rest.
- I cannot stand for more than 10 minutes, and I have radicular pain that goes into my right calf. This matches the pattern of symptoms worsening with standing described in the policy.
- I completed 12 weeks (16 visits) of supervised physical therapy from 2026-04-10 to 2026-07-03, as documented in my physical therapy discharge note.
- I took NSAIDs for 6 months without adequate relief, and I received a corticosteroid injection on 2026-04-20 that gave only 2 weeks of partial relief. Taken together, this is less than clinically meaningful improvement from conservative treatment.
- On exam, I had positive provocative testing on the affected side and a neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged level — findings that fall within the categories the policy lists (e.g., positive straight leg raise/crossed straight leg raise/femoral stretch test, dermatomal sensory deficit, reflex changes, or unremitting radicular pain).
- My MRI from 2026-06-08 shows an L4-L5 disc extrusion with severe right lateral recess stenosis and compression of the traversing L5 nerve root, which is the structural finding correlating with my symptoms and exam findings.
- I have no active infection and no untreated substance use disorder that

evidence.submission_route: Log in at my.cigna.com to find your plan's appeal form and submit it there, or call the number on your card. The mailing address is plan-specific — use the one on your denial letter. Online: my.cigna.com By phone: 1-800-244-6224, or the number on your card Deadline: Usually 180 days from the denial -- but your denial letter is authoritative.
